{"concepts_used":["GC-0102","GC-0113","GC-0097","GC-0138","GC-0093"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part60/4/16/4/16/2","quote":"IP Australia must notify the IB of any opposition within: four months of the publication of acceptance, or seven months of the publication of acceptance where an extension of time for filing Notice of Opposition has been granted."},{"ref":"TMM/Part60/4/17/4/17/2~2","quote":"IP Australia must notify the IB of provisional refusal based on opposition including all the relevant details listed in Rule 17."},{"ref":"TMR1995/r17A.34C","quote":"(1) A person who intends to oppose the extension of protection may request the Registrar to extend: (a) the period for filing a notice of intention to oppose under subregulation 17A.33(1); or (b) the period for filing a statement of grounds and particulars under subregulation 17A.34A(1)."}],"answer":"For an IRDA, the Manual states that IP Australia must notify the International Bureau (IB) of an opposition-based provisional refusal:

- within **four months of publication of acceptance**; or
- within **seven months of publication of acceptance**, where an extension of time for filing the notice of opposition has been granted.

These are **Manual practice** deadlines, and the notification is made by IP Australia to the IB—not by the opponent. [TMM/Part60/4/16/4/16/2; TMM/Part60/4/17/4/17/2~2]

**Legislation:** regulation 17A.34C permits requests to extend the periods for filing a notice of intention to oppose or a statement of grounds and particulars. The supplied legislative passages do not themselves set out the four- or seven-month notification deadlines, so their legislative basis cannot be verified from these extracts alone. [TMR1995/r17A.34C]"}
